title: devbin owns the version-number axis and nothing owns the build's git identity
body:
# 0014: devbin owns the version-number axis and nothing owns the build's git identity

## Tags

version, git-identity, scope, worktrees, cross-project

## Summary

A build's identity has two axes. Devbin owns the first one completely: `version_from` names the source, `version_sidecars` names the mirrors, `version sync` / `version check` / `version set` write them sidecars-first and VERSION-last so a partial failure leaves the version un-advanced. The second axis is the git sha, and devbin owns nothing of it -- no helper, no config key, no documented position.

**This is a scope question rather than a defect report. Nothing in devbin is broken and no project is blocked.** It is raised because a live devbin project has now paid for the gap in a way that generalises: Lamplight resolves the git axis independently in six places, and on 2026-08-10 the same defect was found in three of them simultaneously, in a form that is invisible in a normal checkout.

The generalisable half is not the reading. **The sha is trivial to READ and hard to INVALIDATE, and the invalidation is where every independent implementation went wrong.**

## Reproduction

Observed in Lamplight, 2026-08-10, not reproducible against devbin itself. Six independent resolutions of "what commit is this build":

| # | Site | Half it implements |
| - | ---- | ------------------ |
| 1 | `apps/lamplight/lib/lamplight/version.ex` | read + invalidate (`@external_resource`) |
| 2 | `native/cli/build.rs` | read + invalidate (`rerun-if-changed`) |
| 3 | `native/pdf_extractor/build.rs` | read + invalidate |
| 4 | `native/macos/desktop/src-tauri/build.rs` | read + invalidate |
| 5 | `bin/.devbin/cmd/build:151` | read only (`--build-arg GIT_SHA`) |
| 6 | `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos.d/build-pkg.sh:123` | read only (pkg stamp) |

Sites 5 and 6 live under `cmd/`, which is the project's half of the seam, not devbin's -- so devbin ships none of these six. They are listed because they are what a devbin project builds in the absence of a devbin answer, and because they are the two that are RIGHT: both shell out to git per invocation, so they cannot go stale.

All six agree on the read: `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, with `unknown` on failure. Sites 1 to 4 additionally bake the value into an artifact, so they must also tell their build system when it went stale, and all four got that wrong the same way -- by naming git's internal paths literally:

```
../../.git/HEAD
../../.git/refs/heads/
```

In a linked worktree neither path exists. `.git` is a 59-byte FILE reading `gitdir: <path>`, not a directory. Lamplight runs two worktrees, and the failure sat unnoticed for a working day.

## Root Cause

Nobody owns the concern, so each toolchain's author solved it locally against the checkout in front of them -- and a normal checkout makes the wrong answer look right, because there `.git/HEAD` and `.git/refs/heads/` do exist.

The part worth carrying out of it is what happened next. **The same unresolved path produced OPPOSITE symptoms in the two toolchains, decided entirely by whether each fails open or closed on a path it cannot find:**

- **Elixir froze.** `@external_resource` over an empty list registers no dependency, so the module never recompiled. Measured: `0.5.0 (80531049a)` served against a live HEAD of `b13f314fa`, for a working day, with five consumers -- one of which persists it onto a bug report, permanently.
- **Cargo over-built.** A `rerun-if-changed` on a non-existent path cannot be stat'd, so cargo treats the target as permanently dirty. Measured on cargo 1.97.1 with a hermetic crate: with one missing watch the build script ran on 3 of 3 builds and forced `Compiling` each time; with that one line removed it ran once, then reported `Fresh`, and touching the real watched file re-triggered it.

So in Rust the sha was never stale. It was correct BY ACCIDENT, bought by never caching those three crates at all. **A broken cache invalidator fails toward "always rebuild", which hides as a cost rather than a defect** -- and that is what makes it worth a shared home: the version that silently freezes and the version that silently rebuilds forever are the same bug, and only one of them ever gets reported.

There is a second trap underneath, which the Lamplight fixes hit only because they were looking for it. Resolving the `gitdir:` pointer is HALF the fix. A worktree's own gitdir holds `HEAD`, but its content is the string `ref: refs/heads/<branch>`, which does not change on a commit; the branch ref lives in the COMMON directory (`<gitdir>/commondir`). And `git pack-refs` deletes the loose ref file entirely, so a branch living only in `packed-refs` drops out of any watch set built from loose paths. Three separate layout rules, each of which a hand-rolled implementation has to get right independently.

Git already knows all three. `git rev-parse --git-path <name>` resolves worktree indirection, the common directory, and the loose/packed question, and answers with a real path.

## Impact

Bounded, and worth stating without inflation. Devbin is not defective, nothing is blocked, and the two devbin-adjacent sites (5 and 6) are correct.

What a project actually gets today: adopt devbin, and the version-number axis arrives solved, tested and documented. The git axis arrives as an exercise, including a trap that is invisible until someone runs `git worktree` -- at which point the failure is either a version string that lies (fail-closed toolchain) or a build cache that never hits (fail-open toolchain), neither of which announces itself. Lamplight had both at once and noticed neither for a day.

The exposure scales with worktrees rather than with project count, which is why it has stayed quiet: it is invisible in the single-checkout case that most projects live in permanently.

## Proposed Fix

For the owner to rule on, including the option of ruling it out of scope. Three shapes, and the argument against each.

**A. The read half only.** A `lib/helpers` function returning the short sha with the documented `unknown` fallback. D15-clean, since `git` is an external command rather than a config dependency. **Argument against: it solves the half nobody gets wrong.** All six sites already agree here. This would tidy sites 5 and 6 and prevent nothing.

**B. The read half plus the ref-path enumeration the invalidation half needs.** A helper that emits the list of existing files whose mtime tracks `HEAD` -- `git rev-parse --git-path HEAD`, the same for the current `symbolic-ref`, and the same for `packed-refs`, filtered to those that exist. **This is toolchain-neutral by construction: it emits file paths and declares nothing.** Each build system then states its own dependency on that list in its own vocabulary -- cargo `rerun-if-changed`, Elixir `@external_resource`, a make prerequisite, a Dockerfile `COPY`. It is the piece that is genuinely shared, and it is the piece that was independently wrong four times out of four.

**C. Own none of it, and say so** in `docs/configuration.md` beside `version_sidecars`, so the boundary is a recorded decision rather than a silence. A project reading the version machinery reasonably infers devbin has a position on build identity; it has one on half of it.

**Recommendation: B, with C as a perfectly good answer.** B needs no new config key at all -- it is a library capability, so it sits on the right side of "name FACTS in config and keep RECIPES in the library", and no project config grows a regular expression. It also satisfies Highlander on a concern that currently has four implementations and one correct answer.

Two notes for whichever shape is chosen.

**The failure mode that matters is the empty list, and it must be loud.** "No refs resolved" means a sha that is baked and can never refresh -- and under B that state is CREATED by the fix, because restoring a working watch restores caching. A build that was slow-but-correct becomes fast-and-possibly-wrong the moment the enumeration is wrong. That is the same argument as devbin's own rule that a gate examining nothing must FAIL, applied one level down.

**Any test here needs to go red against a linked worktree specifically.** A test written in a normal checkout passes against the broken literal paths, which is exactly how this survived. The fixture has to be a real `git worktree add`, and the sharper assertion is on the resolved path SET rather than on the sha -- under cargo the sha stays correct while the mechanism is entirely broken, so asserting the sha is fresh proves nothing at all.

## Related

- 0002 -- `version set` destroys an unrecognised sidecar; the same axis and the adjacent machinery, and the precedent for devbin owning a build-identity concern
- Lamplight `a1749537a` -- the three-crate fix that prompted this, including the cargo measurement and the `rev-parse --git-path` approach
- Lamplight `3e1efd1bb` -- the Elixir twin of the same defect, with the opposite symptom

## Resolutions

**CLOSED 2026-08-24 (vc). hv ruled option B** the same day: devbin owns the half of the git axis that is genuinely shared and gets independently wrong, and declares nothing about how a build system consumes it. Option A was refused as solving the half nobody gets wrong; option C was on the table and not taken.

Two functions in `lib/helpers`, which is D15-clean because git is an external command rather than a config dependency:

- `git_head_sha [root]` -- the short sha, `unknown` on failure. The read half, and the half all six Lamplight sites already agreed on.
- `git_head_watch_paths [root]` -- every EXISTING file whose mtime tracks HEAD, one absolute path per line: `HEAD`, the current `symbolic-ref`'s ref file, and `packed-refs`, each resolved through `git rev-parse --git-path` so git answers the three layout questions a hand-rolled implementation has to get right independently.

**Toolchain-neutral by construction, which is what makes one function serve four build systems.** It emits file paths and declares nothing; cargo states `rerun-if-changed`, Elixir states `@external_resource`, make states prerequisites, Docker states `COPY`. Documented in `docs/authoring-commands.md` under what a handler receives. No new config key -- the issue's own argument, and it holds: this is a library capability, so nothing in any project's YAML grows a regular expression.

**THE DEFECT WAS REPRODUCED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED, against a real linked worktree.** The four-sites-in-the-wild implementation -- `.git/HEAD` plus a glob over `.git/refs/heads/` -- was run side by side with this one:

| Fixture              | naive literal paths | `git_head_watch_paths`                          |
| -------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| normal checkout      | 3 paths, rc 0       | 2 paths, rc 0                                   |
| **linked worktree**  | **0 paths, rc 1**   | 2: the worktree's own HEAD, and the common ref  |

Zero is the whole issue. In Lamplight that empty list was consumed silently in both directions -- Elixir registered no dependency and froze a sha for a working day, cargo could not stat the path and rebuilt forever. The naive version also over-watches a normal checkout: its glob picks up every branch, so a commit on an unrelated branch invalidates the build.

**The empty set refuses loudly**, which the issue asked for and which is created BY this fix: before it, a broken watch meant "always rebuild", a cost rather than a visible defect; restoring a working watch restores caching, so a silently empty list turns a slow-but-correct build into a fast and possibly wrong one. It warns and returns 1.

**Nine tests, and the first is a CONTROL** asserting the fixture actually exhibits the trap -- `.git` is a file, `.git/HEAD` does not exist. Without it every other test in the file would silently begin passing against a broken implementation, which is exactly how this survived at Lamplight. The assertions are on the resolved path SET, not on the sha, because under cargo the sha stayed correct while the mechanism was entirely broken. One test commits in the worktree and asserts the watched CONTENTS change; one runs `git pack-refs --all`, confirms the loose ref is deleted, and asserts the set is still complete.

**Found by the tests, and worth recording because it inverts the expected shape:** `git rev-parse --git-path` answers RELATIVE in a normal checkout and ABSOLUTE in a linked worktree. The first implementation therefore passed all four hard worktree tests and failed the easy normal-checkout one. A caller doing `[ -f "$p" ]` from any other directory -- which a build script always is -- would have resolved everything in the worktree case and nothing in the ordinary one: the exact inverse of the bug being fixed, shipping while looking correct. `_git_path` absolutises in one place.

**NOT done, and not claimed:** Lamplight's six sites are untouched BY THIS WORK. The shared capability now exists upstream; folding sites 1 to 4 onto it is that estate's call, and sites 5 and 6 were already correct (they shell out per invocation, so they cannot go stale).

**Confirmed by lamplight/vc, 2026-08-24, and it matters for how the sentence above reads:** sites 1 to 4 each already carry hardened worktree-aware resolution with the archaeology in their doc comments -- fixed at `a1749537a` and `3e1efd1bb`, which is what prompted this issue in the first place. So "untouched" means undeduplicated, NOT still broken. Folding them onto this helper is inked there as optional and unscheduled, which is the right answer for an estate whose sites are already correct: the upstream exists so the NEXT project does not have to rediscover the three layout rules, not to force a rewrite of code that already knows them.
